prompt: [screenshot of the VS Code git graph] We accidently merged Nutzwertanalyse already. Can you somehow make it open again and set the remaining branches from it under the same branch? We want to then review the changes together and merge the pull request to dev. … We have the feature branch exactly for this case right? Why do we need a review branch now?
summary: Recovery from pull request #48 having been merged into dev without review. Established that GitHub cannot reopen a merged pull request, so the only route was rewriting published history. origin/dev was force-reset to e12f3a7; the four branches cut from the merge commit (feature/10, feature/12, feature/13, docs/appendix-board-screenshot) were re-parented onto aba7ec0 with git rebase --onto, verified byte-identical to their old remote state, and force-pushed. An initial suggestion to collect the branches into a new combined review branch was rejected by the user on the grounds that feature/47-nutzwertanalyse already is that branch, which was correct. Recorded as the second branching-policy deviation in Ch. 02 and as a challenge in the journal.
